subject: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & integration follow-up

Subject: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & integration follow-up

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps below so we stay aligned: 

Recap:
- Goal: Dedicated capacity for conversational assistants + reranking/embeddings pipelines.
- Primary SLOs: p95 latency target ~350ms for short prompts (~256 tokens), batch/async allowed for reranker workloads.
- Traffic profile: mostly bursty during business hours, some scheduled batch jobs overnight (Peter to share numbers).

Integration / Tech items we flagged:
- SDK setup & auth: token-based API keys, support for short-lived tokens (recommended), and service-account flows for server-to-server.
- Routing: ability to pin specific routes to dedicated pool + fallback to hosted model variants.
- Structured output & tool-calling: want deterministic JSON outputs and tool calling support for a set of internal tools.
- Embeddings & rerankers: embeddings indexes will be hosted externally; reranker model will run in Dedicated — need to size for both online QPS and periodic re-embed batches.

Dedicated capacity sizing follow-ups we need from you: 
1) Confirm peak QPS (inference calls/sec) and average tokens per request (you mentioned ~300 tokens average).
2) Concurrent live sessions target (approx. how many simultaneous users invoking chat endpoints).
3) Nightly batch/throughput requirements for re-indexing (jobs per hour, throughput).

Next steps (proposed):
- Peter to send traffic estimates and architecture diagram (Can you attach the diagram and a spreadsheet with QPS by hour?) — target: EOD Monday.
- Redwood to produce a sizing and autoscaling proposal + queue sizing recommendations — will share by 4/28.
- Tech deep-dive (architecture + auth + routing + tool-calling) on 5/3.

Attachments: none from our side yet; we’ll attach the sizing doc after we incorporate your numbers.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — attaching what Peter and I put together. High level here: 

- Peak QPS: ~150 inference requests/sec for the chat endpoint (10:30–11:30 PST daily peak).
- Average tokens per request: ~280 (we're seeing a 75/25 split short/long where long pushes to ~800 tokens).
- Concurrent live users: expect ~25–40 concurrent sessions hitting the chat endpoint (each session may do rapid-turn exchanges).
- Reranker/embeddings: Online reranker traffic ~20 QPS during working hours; daily reindex batch processes ~500k docs over 6 hours at night.
- Security: we need support for customer-managed keys (KMS) and audit logs for inference calls.

See attached: acme-traffic-estimates.xlsx and a simple architecture diagram (acme-arch-diagram.png).

We’d prefer a Dedicated setup with private networking (VPC) and the ability to pin the reranker to dedicated nodes.

Let us know if any of that needs clarification. Looking forward to your sizing doc before the deep-dive.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity: autoscaling & integration follow-up (internal notes)

Marissa —

I pulled together an initial sizing + architecture notes based on Acme's numbers (150 peak QPS chat, 25–40 concurrent sessions, 20 QPS reranker, nightly 500k doc reindex over 6 hours). Key recommendations below: 

1) Cluster baseline & autoscale:
- Start with a baseline pool of 4 dedicated inference nodes (N1) sized for low-latency chat (each node ~ supports ~40–50 concurrent lightweight streams depending on model/quantization).
- Configure autoscaling to add up to 8 nodes on sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 70% for 3+ minutes or queue depth > 250. Scale-down to baseline after 10 minutes of under-utilization.

2) Concurrency and queue sizing: 
- Concurrency per GPU: assume 40 concurrent “live” chat streams per GPU for the target model with 256–512 token context when using AMP/FP16/quantized runtimes.
- Queue: add a request queue with per-route capacity control. For the chat route, provision initial queue depth 1000 requests, with SLA-based ingress throttling to protect tail latency.

3) Throughput for reranker & batch jobs:
- Run reranker as separate service-backed pool (2 nodes) pinned to Dedicated; autoscale to 4 nodes for spikes.
- For batch reindexing, run jobs on worker nodes with higher throughput; schedule during off-peak window and throttle to avoid saturating storage/ingress.

4) Routing, auth, SDK: 
- Recommend service-account short-lived tokens for server-to-server calls and rotating API keys for human/service access.
- Use route-pinning: chat -> chat-pool (baseline nodes), reranker -> reranker-pool (pinned), fallback policy to hosted small-model variant if Dedicated capacity exhausted.
- SDK: include built-in token refresh, retry/backoff, and optional structured-output parsing helper for tool-calling.

5) Observability & SLOs:
- Instrument per-token latency and per-request queue wait time. Set alerts at p95 queue wait > 150ms or p95 latency > 400ms.

Known caveats: exact concurrency depends on chosen model, quantization, and KV cache size — we'll need to pick model variant during the deep-dive.

I attached a short sizing spreadsheet and a PDF proposal draft (I'll hand this to you as the final proposal).

—Aditya

Hi Sara / Peter —

Thanks for the data and diagram. Attached is our initial sizing + proposal (redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf) reflecting Aditya's recommendations. Highlights:

- Baseline: 4 dedicated nodes for chat-pool, autoscale up to 8 for bursts.
- Reranker: dedicated 2-node pool, autoscale to 4 as needed.
- Queue policy: per-route queue with 1,000 request depth, SLA throttles to keep p95 latency under control.
- Auth: support for short-lived service tokens + KMS integration (we will need your KMS provider details during onboarding).
- Structured output/tool-calling: SDK will include helpers for deterministic JSON parsing + tool invocation hooks.

Proposed next step: Tech deep-dive on 2027-05-03 at 11:00 AM PST (60 min) to finalize model variant, quantization tradeoffs, and deploy plan. Can you confirm that time works and that we should include your security contact for the KMS/audit discussion?
